concept.name: Elder Ray index
concept.definition: Alexander Elder's two-part oscillator: Bull Power = period high minus a 13-period EMA of closes, and Bear Power = period low minus the same EMA, measuring how far buyers and sellers can push price above and below the market's consensus of value.
concept.intuition: The EMA is the agreed value; the high shows the maximum buyers could reach and the low the maximum sellers could reach - their distances from the EMA are the two camps' power.
concept.mechanics: Compute EMA(13) of the close; Bull Power = High - EMA13 (typically positive in uptrends) and Bear Power = Low - EMA13 (typically negative). Elder's buy setup: EMA rising with Bear Power negative but rising; sell/short setup: EMA falling with Bull Power positive but falling.
concept.formula: Bull Power = High - EMA(Close, 13); Bear Power = Low - EMA(Close, 13).
concept.failure_modes: Moving-average-based, so it lags and whipsaws around zero - both limitations Investopedia lists explicitly - and signals in fast reversals arrive after much of the move.
concept.misconceptions: Positive Bull Power alone is not a buy - Elder's rules require the EMA slope plus the opposing camp weakening (Bear Power below zero and rising), not one component in isolation.
concept.example: With the 13-day EMA at 50, a bar's high of 51.5 and low of 48.5 give Bull Power +1.5 and Bear Power -1.5; Bear Power rising from -2.0 to -1.0 while the EMA climbs is Elder's buy configuration.

citations.source: Elder-Ray Index Definition and Uses - Investopedia
